channel.title: The Brilliant Employee
channel.description: One person, one automation system, and the workplace built around it so the work can be trusted.

item.title: My Learning Loop Had a Sign Error. It Would Have Rewarded Failure With More Work
item.description: A weighted term inverted an escalation rule. A controlled sweep found it before the loop was ever connected to live behaviour. A unit test could not have.

item.title: My Security Gate Has Caught 34 False Alarms and Zero Attacks. I Kept It Anyway
item.description: A guard against prompt injection, measured on a real machine. All 34 flags were ordinary reading. Six sessions lost their outbound tools mid-run, and one of them was mine.

item.title: My Task Log Records What the AI Spent. Two Extra Fields Record Whether It Was Worth It
item.description: Cost and latency price a task. They cannot say whether the money bought anything. Two fields can, and no instrumentation standard carries the second one.

item.title: A Hardcoded 4 in My Reporting Tool Erased Every Win the Expensive Model Earned
item.description: One program seeded each model differently. The other assumed they were identical. The subtraction clamped to zero, so every report showed no wins at all.

item.title: Every Nightly Backup Was Dead. I Still Cannot Tell You How Many There Were
item.description: Scheduled jobs died at startup under a macOS permission wall, before writing a line. With no logs, three of my own records disagree on the count and nothing can settle it.

item.title: My Model Router Picked the Same Model 5,000 Times Out of 5,000
item.description: Thirty days of my own tests said the router worked. The first benchmark I did not write showed it had stopped choosing. The cause was a good rule with nothing to feed it.

item.title: My Review Queue Reported Zero Remaining. An Analytics Job Had Eaten It
item.description: A queue printed zero unadjudicated for days. That is what a finished queue prints and what a starved one prints. Telling them apart needs a counter the queue does not own.

item.title: My Router Recommended the Cheap Model 89% of the Time. The Expensive One Ran Anyway
item.description: A triage step sized 89% of tasks to the cheapest model. I quoted it as a cost result for five weeks. Joining it against the execution log showed the advice was followed twice in 816 runs.

item.title: My AI Security Scanner Reported a Leak in a File That Does Not Exist
item.description: An AI subagent reported leaked GitHub tokens at a path with no file. The address was invented and the credential type was not. How to tell those apart by counting.

item.title: I Told My AI Agents Not to Commit to Git. They Did It Anyway, So I Stopped Using Words
item.description: A rule written into a prompt is advice that competes with everything else in the context. A program on the tool boundary is a control. Six of mine sit there, and four can refuse.
